name: NY-16
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+18 district lean in a heavily Democratic Westchester-area seat
Incumbent George Latimer's name recognition and $660K war chest versus a challenger with no reported fundraising
Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 98%
No public polling or expert ratings flag the race as competitive
model.rationale: The district's D+18 partisan lean, Latimer's incumbency advantages, and a Republican challenger with no visible fundraising or outside support all point the same direction, and markets price a Democratic win at roughly 98 percent. With no polls or expert ratings suggesting any competitiveness, the fundamentals-based estimate of a roughly 24-point Democratic margin stands.
model.watch: Any late polling showing a single-digit race, or a sudden infusion of challenger fundraising or outside spending, would be the first sign this safe seat deserves a second look.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
New York's 16th District, anchored in Westchester County, carries a strong Democratic lean of D+18. George Latimer, the Democratic incumbent, is seeking another term after winning the seat in 2024. He has raised roughly $660,000 for the cycle, while Republican Joseph Cinquemani shows no reported fundraising and no outside spending on either side.

No independent public polls cover the general election, and no expert raters have flagged the race as competitive. Prediction markets price a Democratic victory at about 98 percent. The combination of a deep district lean, incumbency, and an underfunded challenger places this firmly in Safe D territory. The main caveat is the absence of polling, so the assessment rests on district fundamentals rather than direct measurement, but nothing in the available evidence suggests genuine competition.
